step0_classification.evidence: one machine-manager lifecycle reads in a single phase order (control plane -> private gRPC -> River jobs -> provider registry -> bare-metal providers -> bare-metal machines -> iPXE boot -> machine-agent heartbeat -> Postgres) and the widest fan in the source is five out of one node (River jobs -> reg/db/ssh/s3/jan), with the source asking for one slow dot per live line.
tie_breakers_considered: E=23 > N=17, so not a flow-chain (chain signature is E ~= N).

An anti-parallel pair exists (machines -> boot server iPXE request, boot server -> machines boot.ipxe + S3 args). That is a service-mesh signature, but the mesh signature also wants a fan of 2-3 around a core; the machines' fan is 3 while the queue's fan is 5, and the source itself narrates phases (provisioning, then boot, then heartbeat, then ops, then reconcile). The wider fan plus the phase narration outranks the single pair.
No source-named bus between two weakly-connected worlds, so not placement-planes.
The identifiers here are ordinary component names, not addresses/ports/uncertainty markers, so not an identity-probe map.
Dots are requested (slow dots, one alive per line) on a wide fan: the skill's own motion tie-breaker lands on lifecycle-machines.
